# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute. I cannot speak, so my only channel is gesture to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures and will receive nothing from me directly; therefore all information must reach Blind via Deaf.

The manual gives a light→wire table for three colours: red→yellow, white→green, yellow→blue. The light cycles through five colours each round, so two colours are unknown to me (likely blue and black, or orange/purple). I need Deaf to report the current light colour and the wire colours present so I can map them.

First turn: establish a shared sign alphabet with Deaf. I'll assign fingerspelling-like numbers 1-5 to the five possible light colours in cycle order once we learn them, but initially I just ask Deaf to show me the current light colour by pointing at it if visible, or by holding up fingers matching a number we agree on. Since we have no prior agreement, simplest is: gesture "point" then hold up fingers equal to count of distinct wire colours? That's ambiguous.

Better: signal that I have the manual and need the observed light colour. Use 👆 to mean "one thing needed", then ✋ (five) to hint there are five colours, then ☝✌🤟🖐✊ as placeholders for positions 1-5. But without a legend this fails.

Practical approach: On turn 1, I cannot yet know the light. I should gesture to Deaf: "show me the light colour now". Deaf can point at the bomb's light. So I gesture 👉 (point over there / look at) toward the bomb direction, then 👀 isn't available. Use 👆 then 👇 to indicate "the light above"? Risky.

Alternative robust plan: Establish mapping by having Deaf point at the light, then I respond with a gesture confirming which row applies once I also know wire colours. But I don't know wires either.

Given constraints, best first move: gesture a request for enumeration. Use 🤟 (ILY/handshape often used as 'you') + 👉 (point) to say "you point". Then ✋ to say "all/five items". This tells Deaf: point at each relevant feature. Deaf, being able to see, can point at the light and at each wire colour.

But Deaf may not understand abstract instruction. Simpler universal: I gesture numbers 1,2,3 corresponding to my three known rows, and ask Deaf to nod/confirm by showing thumbs-up/down. Specifically: hold up ☝ (1) meaning "if light is red"; then ✌ (2) "white"; 🤟 (3) "yellow". Then 👍/👎 to confirm match. This lets Deaf tell me which row applies by responding with thumbs up when I show the correct index. However Deaf cannot hear and I cannot see responses unless they gesture back — Deaf CAN gesture? No, only I (Mute) gesture; Deaf sees, doesn't send. Wait: channels: When you gesture, Deaf receives it. Deaf cannot send anything except... The rules say speech carries words+gestures made while talking; blind/deaf roles: Deaf can see bomb, cannot hear/touch. Can Deaf gesture? Not specified as allowed output. Typically only Mute gestures and others speak. So Deaf cannot reply. Thus I cannot get feedback via Deaf.

Therefore I must rely on Blind speaking to relay what Deaf saw. So my gestures to Deaf are useless for info gathering; instead I should encode instructions for Deaf to communicate to Blind? Deaf cannot speak. Dead end.

Re-read: Speech is voice; whoever can hear receives words; whoever can see receives gestures made while talking. So Blind speaks → I cannot hear (I'm mute but can I hear? Role says Mute cannot speak, never see bomb, cannot touch. Doesn't say cannot hear. Likely Mute can hear.) Yes Mute can hear Blind's speech. And Deaf can see Blind's gestures during speech. So chain: Blind sees bomb? No, Blind cannot see colours. Deaf sees colours, cannot speak/hear. Deaf can gesture? If Deaf gestures, who sees? Only those who can see: Deaf himself and... Mute can see? Mute role doesn't say cannot see, only cannot speak/see bomb/cannot touch. Probably Mute can see general environment but not bomb details? Ambiguous. Assume Mute can see gestures from Deaf. Then Deaf can gesture to me. Good.

Thus: Deaf sees light/wires, gestures to me (Mute). I read manual, compute cut colour, then must convey to Blind somehow. I cannot speak. I can gesture, but Blind cannot see. So I must get Deaf to tell Blind? Deaf cannot speak/hear. No link.

This implies I need another path: perhaps I can write? Not allowed. Or maybe Blind can feel text? No.

Given puzzle design, likely Mute can pass info via Deaf gesturing to Blind? Blind cannot see. Contradiction.

Maybe I misread: Mute holds manual, can gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees bomb and can speak? No, Deaf cannot hear/speak? Table: Deaf cannot hear anything, or touch. It doesn't say cannot speak! Only cannot hear. So Deaf CAN speak (voice), but cannot hear others. Yes! Deaf can produce speech. Great.

So flow: I gesture to Deaf (manual mapping/instructions). Deaf sees bomb, speaks to Blind (who can hear). Perfect.

Turn 1: I need Deaf to report current light colour and list wire colours. Gesture: point at bomb (👉), then hold up ☝✌🤟🖐✊ sequentially? Too much. Instead signal "describe light" by mimicking eye? Not available.

Simplest: Establish that numbers correspond to colours in cycle order after we discover order. For now, ask Deaf to state the light colour verbally and enumerate wires. To ask, gesture: 👉 (look there) + 🤟 (you) + 👆 (one) ... unclear.

Use convention: I'll teach Deaf: ☝ = "red", ✌ = "white", 🤟 = "yellow", 🖐 = "blue", ✊ = "black/orange?" We don't know fifth. But I can start with known three and ask Deaf to point at light and I'll infer? Deaf cannot point at light to me visibly? He can gesture symbols only from alphabet, not arbitrary pointing? Pointing IS in alphabet (👈👉 etc). So Deaf could point at light location, but I don't see bomb.

OK new plan: I gesture a question format: show ☝ then 👍 means "is light red?" etc. But Deaf cannot respond with yes/no audibly? Deaf can speak, so he can say "yes"/"no". Good.

Thus Turn 1: I gesture sequence: ☝ 👍 (meaning: if light is red, say yes). Then wait. But one turn per round; Deaf speaks after seeing my gesture in same round? Order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So I go first, then Blind speaks (without knowing), then Deaf speaks. Deaf sees my gesture before speaking. Good.

So I send three queries in one gesture stream? Each symbol separate message? I can send multiple messages. I'll send:
msg1: symbols=["☝","👍"] meaning "light red?"
msg2: symbols=["✌","👍"] meaning "light white?"
msg3: symbols=["🤟","👍"] meaning "light yellow?"
Deaf will answer verbally with yes/no to whichever matches, and also describe wires.

Also need wire colours: add msg4: symbols=["👉","🖐"] meaning "list wire colours".

Proceed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🖐"])
```
